# Library bindings and project profile: the layering ADR
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #152, sha256:d6904e19f3b4e214c04cf05e4a83cf4afec4388ebda3b0fa04ce06e0dabf314b). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** docs (thin slice; an ADR extending the extension map)
- **Milestone:** Purpose: verifiability, preserved intent and reviewability
- **Source:** Product direction (purpose level), 2026-10-28 (VISION ruling 7: Phrase is not meant to beat C#; it solves the problems of AI-written code being unaccountable, unverifiable at the speed it is written, with intent vanishing with the prompt) and Decider D99 (Codex Yes, Grok Support-it). The head-to-head benchmark stays published as context and is not the success measure.
- **Depends on:** 138
- **Story:** As Dana, I want a written layering of extension, adapter, library binding and project profile, so that the same spec can come out as FastEndpoints today and as Minimal APIs or controllers later without changing a spec.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given the ADR, When it is read, Then it defines the layers: domain extensions define abstract concepts (endpoint, route, store), library bindings under each adapter map them to a concrete library (web plus C# to FastEndpoints by default, Minimal APIs or controllers as possible; data to EF Core or Dapper), a project profile file selects the bindings, the architecture style (vertical slices, clean or onion) and the coding standards (naming, nullable, analyzers, file layout, test framework), with smart defaults and an override; deterministic emitters and an LLM-as-compiler both honour it; the same spec and generated tests verify every binding
  2. Given the C# emitter today, When it is audited, Then the ADR lists every place FastEndpoints is wired in (the project template, Program.cs, the endpoint classes, effectful generated specs calling Factory.Create, the test helpers and the benchmark scorers of cards 110 and 111) and names the seam each needs, plus a rule for what the prototype path and later cards may and may not hard-wire so a second binding is never blocked
  3. Given the layering, When the ADR is read, Then it says a second binding is built only on a real need and the default stays FastEndpoints with no hard-coding in the specs

## Context

- Docs only. Extends docs/adr/ADR-extension-map.md (card 141). Principle: library preferences, architecture style and coding standards need a deliberate design, because a project's choices should be data the emitters honour and not code they hard-wire.
